name: Cleveland Hopkins International Airport
before:
Ohio's largest and busiest airport, nine miles south west of downtown Cleveland, with non-stop service to 43 destinations and a catchment of 4.9 million people. It sits next to NASA's Glenn Research Center.

It has a longer list of firsts than almost any airport in America. It was the first anywhere with an air traffic control tower, the first with a two level design separating arrivals from departures, and the first in North America connected directly to a rail transit line. It was founded on 1 July 1925 and turned a hundred in July 2025.

The market shape is the useful part for pricing. United ran a hub here and closed it in 2014, which opened the door to low cost carriers in what had been one of the most expensive markets in the country. Traffic recovered within a few years, and United is still the largest carrier by passengers even without the hub.

The terminal dates from 1978 and was renovated in 2016. Three of its four concourses are in use.
after:
Ohio's busiest airport, a 12-mile drive south west of downtown Cleveland. The airport says it has nonstop flights to more than 40 destinations. It sits next to NASA's Glenn Research Center.

Cleveland Hopkins opened on 1 July 1925 and has a long list of firsts. It was the first anywhere with an air traffic control tower and the first with a two level design separating arrivals from departures. In 1968 it became the first airport in North America connected directly to a rail transit line.

United ran a hub here and closed it in 2014, which opened the door to low cost carriers. Traffic recovered within a few years, and United is still the largest carrier by passengers even without the hub.

Airlines use three concourses, A, B and C.

claims.claim: a 12-mile drive from downtown Cleveland
claims.note: Was 'nine miles'. The figures differ by measure: Wikipedia 9 miles, the Encyclopedia of Cleveland History 8 miles from Public Square, 10.0 miles in a straight line from the GeoNames centre, and the operator a 12-mile drive. The operator's drive distance is used, as the airport's own figure and the one a traveller meets; it passes the coordinates check (12 / 10.0 = 1.2). Nine miles also passes (0.9), so this is a choice of measure, not a correction of an error.

claims.claim: CLEvolution works under way from July 2026
claims.why: Held back: new, replaces nothing. The operator broke ground on 1 July 2026 on the Gold Lot (about 1,600 spaces), the first project of CLEvolution, its multi-year terminal modernisation; it says the airport stays fully operational through construction. Wikipedia gives the programme as $1.6 billion, with a new terminal building targeted for 2032. Worth adding if Andy wants the works mentioned: parking and roads will change over several years.
